settings.welcomeStep1: Choose this computer's role: the main one has the keyboard and mouse, the others are controlled.
settings.welcomeStep2: The secret must be the same on every computer: copy the main computer's secret to the controlled ones.
settings.welcomeStep3: Controlled computers find the main one on their own on the local network. Otherwise, enter its address in “Connect to”.
settings.welcomeEnd: Save: Baskul restarts with these settings.
settings.configUnreadable: The configuration file cannot be read

machine.title: This computer
machine.primaryDesc: The keyboard and mouse are plugged into this computer: it controls the others.
machine.secondaryDesc: This computer is controlled from the main computer.
machine.name: Display name
machine.nameHelp: Optional. Defaults to the computer's name.

connection.intro: The main computer waits for the controlled ones; each controlled computer connects to it.
connection.addressHelp: Controlled computers find it on their own on the local network; otherwise, enter this address in their “Connect to”.
connection.connectHelp: IP address or .local name of the main computer. Empty: found automatically.
connection.secretHelp: Same on every computer (at least 12 characters).
connection.newSecretWarning: The new secret must also be copied to the other computers.
connection.listenHelp: Address and port the controlled computers connect to. Rarely needs changing.
connection.activityHelp: This computer stays active while you are active on another one: no display sleep or screen saver, “active” status in Teams, Discord… When you step away, it notices too. Turn it on on every computer.
connection.announceHelp: Automatic discovery (Bonjour): controlled computers find this one without typing an address.
connection.discoveryHelp: Finds the main computer on the local network (Bonjour).
connection.foundHelp: “Choose” sets its address below. Otherwise, Baskul connects to the one with the same secret.
connection.interfaceHelp: The one Baskul uses (Ethernet rather than Wi-Fi, for example).

switching.goToSecondary: Go to the last controlled computer
switching.goToSecondaryHelp: The cursor comes back where it was, on the last controlled computer used.
switching.returnHereHelp: The same shortcut as above lets you go back and forth.
switching.hotkeysNeeded: Without edge switching, these two shortcuts are required.
switching.edgesHelp: Pushing the mouse against a screen edge moves to the neighbouring computer in the layout.
switching.positionHelp: Side of this computer where a controlled computer connecting for the first time is placed.
switching.cornersHelp: In the corners, the edge does not switch computers (a window's ✕ button…). 0 = none.
switching.lockHelp: Locks or unlocks the cursor on the screen where it is.
switching.nextHelp: Moves to the next computer: the main one, then the controlled ones in layout order.

mouse.scrollingHelp: By line, like a Windows mouse wheel; by pixel, more precise; smooth, animated and accelerated like Mac Mouse Fix (macOS).
mouse.smoothSpeedHelp: Distance per notch; notches close together go further.
mouse.smoothnessHelp: How long scrolling glides after each notch. Same settings as Mac Mouse Fix.
mouse.precisionHelp: A single notch scrolls only 10 pixels; quick notches still accelerate (Mac Mouse Fix option).
mouse.trackpadHelp: Scrolling is sent as a trackpad gesture followed by its momentum: bounce at the end of pages, momentum handled by apps… (Mac Mouse Fix option).
mouse.sideButtonsHelp: Buttons for Chrome, Firefox, VS Code… “Swipe” gesture for Safari, Finder, Xcode…

keyboard.mediaKeysHelp: Volume, playback…: on the computer where the cursor is, on the main computer, or on the last controlled computer used.

clipboard.sensitiveHelp: Passwords copied from a password manager.
clipboard.filesHelp: Copied in the Finder or Explorer, they are copied to the computer where you paste them.
clipboard.maxSizeHelp: Images are sent in their original format (PNG, JPEG, GIF…).

interface.trayIconHelp: Icon in the menu bar or notification area. Monochrome: matches the other system icons.
interface.bubbleHelp: The computer's name shows briefly next to the cursor when the keyboard and mouse arrive on it.

advanced.isoSwapHelp: European (ISO) Mac keyboards swap these two keys compared to a PC keyboard. “Auto” corrects this based on the Mac's keyboard: only change it if they stay swapped.
advanced.commandsHelp: For other apps (Keyboard Maestro, Shortcuts, AutoHotkey…): the keyboard and mouse move to this computer (here), to the main one (primary), to the next one (next) or to a controlled computer by name (switch Studio); toggle goes back and forth. “status” shows Baskul's state. “Copy” gives the full command, with Baskul's path:
advanced.updatesHelp: Looks for new versions and downloads them; a restart installs them.

settings.linuxNotice: On Linux, Baskul does not share the keyboard and mouse yet: these settings have no effect here.

layout.title: Screen layout
layout.help: Place the controlled computers around this one, like your screens on the desk: you move from one to the other through their shared edge.
layout.dragHint: Drag a controlled computer onto a cell, or click it to select it.
layout.pickHint: Click a free cell to move the selected computer there, or drag it.
layout.hotkeyHelp: The keyboard and mouse move straight to this computer.
layout.isolated: “{names}” touches no other computer: only a shortcut leads there. | “{names}” touch no other computer: only shortcuts lead there.

about.tagline: One keyboard, one mouse and a shared clipboard across several computers.
about.thanksText: Built with Rust, Tauri, Vue and Naive UI. Smooth scrolling follows the algorithm of Mac Mouse Fix, by Noah Nuebling.

update.title: Updates
update.availableManual: Version {version} is available: download it from the releases page.
update.ready: Version {version} downloaded: restart Baskul to install it.
update.readyText: Restart to install the new version; this window reopens afterwards.
update.unsavedText: They will be lost. Restart anyway?
